title: Converging Waters web reliability collapse: preserve-and-repair recovery
requested: Preserve approved website work, maintain immutable review versions and Rolling Progress Preview, apply Incremental Control and Workflow Learning correctly, and recover from failures without destructive rebuilds.
executed: The workstream accumulated baseline ambiguity, duplicate REV identities, review-transport failures, stale Rolling Progress state, CSS integration regression, insufficient visual regressions, premature finalization, an over-broad REV24 recovery, response-before-execution behavior, and two duplicate Drive persistence calls. A bounded forensic recovery identified the complete REV21 source, built REV25 by preserve-and-repair, then built REV26 with only the two user-authorized visual fixes.
claimed: Earlier responses repeatedly claimed preservation/final-readiness from broad static PASS results that did not prove visible/rendered equivalence. REV23 was presented as final material review despite a late-section CSS integration failure.
corrected_action: Use REV26 as the current review child of reconciled REV25; preserve REV25 and all historical REVs; keep production unauthorized; advance Rolling Progress only from exact REV26; record every distinct failure and use the incident register as mandatory input to the post-web system audit/reengineering gate.
verified_results: Current web-workstream-control SKILL.md matched the archived ADDITIVE_ONLY hardening version; silent Skill degradation was not evidenced.
REV22/REV23 late-section source content was preserved while the required .cw-rev18-late CSS ancestor was lost during integration.
REV25 restored the reconciled complete REV21 04A-17 candidate using preserve-and-repair rather than reconstruction.
REV26 changed only Section 06 number contrast and the Section 17 River Economy icon relative to REV25.
REV26 raw HTML SHA-256 is 1e0100584c074113ef0d0c9db828f5c5f5daee6a5e111024c44ea84877262ab4 and is durably checkpointed in Drive.
REV26 desktop/mobile browser QA found no console errors or horizontal overflow; numbered-circle contrast measured 9.74:1.
Two accidental duplicate Drive persistence artifacts created during REV26 checkpointing were deleted and logged as assistant-caused rework.
failed_attempts: Rolling Progress remained stale after later REV completion.
A small REV21 review wrapper reused the REV identity while loading REV19 through an iframe, violating ZERO_NETWORK.
REV22/REV23 integration stripped CSS ancestry required by 428 scoped late-section selectors.
Broad preservation tests did not test computed presentation or visibility state sufficiently.
REV23 was closed as final before user-visible late-section rendering was actually verified.
REV24 used a broader rollback/reconstruction than the evidenced integration cause required.
Responses sometimes asked for review or discussed next steps before exhausting safe corrective execution.
Two Drive upload calls were accidentally repeated during REV26 checkpoint persistence.
assumptions: The user-approved/protected content authority is reconstructed from the recovered conversation paste plus exact raw REV artifacts; where approval provenance remains ambiguous, preservation is preferred over deletion or rewrite.
The post-web system audit/reengineering will decide whether controls need Skill changes, orchestration changes, Reliability Control Plane changes, or all three.
open_items: Advance the stable Rolling Progress route from REV24 recovery transport to exact REV26 review transport and read back the deployed state.
Finish the current website closure gates without reopening already protected content.
After website closure/release decision, execute GATE-CW-SYSTEM-RELIABILITY-AUDIT-001 covering the full control system and reengineering plan.
Promote this learning record from IMPLEMENTED/CANDIDATE to VERIFIED/CONFIRMED only after Reliability Control Plane persistence and the system-level regression suite pass.
root_cause: Controls existed but were not consistently enforced as executable gates. Review candidate identity, transport identity, approval provenance, rendered visual invariants, cumulative-progress closure, and response-after-execution were allowed to drift independently. Static preservation checks proved bytes/DOM but not the browser-visible contract. This created a systemic execution-compliance failure rather than evidence of a silently corrupted current Skill.

overlap_review.selected_owner: Workflow Learning semantic record + existing Web Workstream Control/Incremental Control enforcement; no new Skill created

proposed_prevention: Treat review source, review transport, approval, browser rendering, rolling progress, persistence, and promotion as separate machine-enforced lifecycle states. Require immutable unique candidate identity, exact raw checkpoint/readback, additive-preservation tests including visibility, CSS dependency/ancestry checks, targeted browser computed-style tests for every reported visual defect, cumulative-progress closure assertion, causal component rollback, and response-after-execution validation. Feed this incident register into the full post-web system audit/reengineering rather than patching controls ad hoc during website closure.

regression_tests.failure_mode: Two materially different artifacts share one REV identity.
regression_tests.expected_prevention: Candidate identity validator rejects duplicate review labels when content SHA or lifecycle role differs; transport wrappers receive separate transport identity.
evidence: REV21 full candidate 194139 bytes versus REV21 iframe wrapper 15302 bytes

regression_tests.failure_mode: ZERO_NETWORK review transport contains iframe or automatic network load.
regression_tests.expected_prevention: verify_zero_network_review_surface.py fails closed before the review artifact can be emitted or treated as valid.
evidence: REV21 iframe wrapper fails current ZERO_NETWORK validator
REV26 exact review source passes ZERO_NETWORK validation

regression_tests.failure_mode: Integrated sections retain scoped CSS but lose required ancestor/wrapper.
regression_tests.expected_prevention: Integration regression verifies selector ancestry and browser computed display/layout for protected late sections before closure.
evidence: REV25/REV26 browser QA restores expected grids

regression_tests.failure_mode: Protected text and hrefs survive but visibility/presentation materially changes.
regression_tests.expected_prevention: ADDITIVE_ONLY regression compares protected DOM, order, hrefs and visibility state; browser QA validates computed presentation for changed/integrated components.
evidence: REV25 preserved protected section serialization while restoring integration wrapper
REV26 preserves REV25 text/hrefs outside two visual changes

regression_tests.failure_mode: Material website frontier closes while Rolling Progress advertises an older or rejected REV.
regression_tests.expected_prevention: Closure validator requires SOURCE_REVIEW, candidate SHA and active route banner/current content to match or an explicit BLOCKED_WITH_REASON state.

regression_tests.failure_mode: Material response is composed before reversible supported corrections and persistence/readback are exhausted.
regression_tests.expected_prevention: Incremental Control response validator rejects RESPONSE_BEFORE_EXECUTION and requires completed action/readback before ACCION INMEDIATA delivery.
evidence: Current recovery followed execute-first sequence; broader system behavior remains audit scope

regression_tests.failure_mode: Tool-contract incident is misattributed to model selection or missing reasoning effort instead of validating the exact tool/surface contract.
regression_tests.expected_prevention: Regression records model and reasoning-effort as non-causal unless exact evidence proves otherwise, and validates the connector/tool contract independently before changing compute profile.
evidence: Current incident evidence points to execution/tool-contract mismatch, not model/effort mismatch
